To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the perfusate used for hypothermic machine perfusion of the liver is not relevant for the induction of ER stress and that the induction of ER‐stress by hypothermic perfusion can be attenuated by oxygenation.

1) Endoplasmic stress‐mediated apoptosis is triggered in livers during hypothermic machine perfusion, 2) The effect is independent of perfusion medium and oxygen, 3) The simple insufflation with gaseous oxygen may represent an alternative to hypothermic machine oxygenation, and 4) The effect of perfusion medium on ER‐stress‐induced apoptosis remains to be elucidated.

the endoplasmatic stress activation is conjecture a specific side effect to long‐term machine perfusion irrespective of the perfusion medium, actually promoting the cellular apoptosis via activation the caspase‐ 12.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of perfusates, perfusion and the effect of oxygenation on endoplasmic stress‐induced apoptosis in the graft during hypothermic machine liver preservation.
the role of perfusates and oxygen supply for ER‐stress and cell death after hypoxic storage of the liver.
the role of the perfusate and perfusion itself in ER‐stress‐induced cell damage during hypothermic machine perfusion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the endoplasmatic reticulum is not a specific target for cold preservation injury.
perfusion medium, continuous oxygenation and rheology of the graft are all relevant factors to be considered in order to avoid the detrimental effects of machine perfusion.
the perfusate itself, the perfusion process and the presence of O2 are all involved in the induction of ER‐stress in livers after hypothermic preservation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the perfusion medium is of minor importance for liver viability after hypothermic preservation.
perfusion itself, independent of the medium, is a major factor for endoplasmatic stress induction and subsequent cell death after hypotermic machine preservation.
the endoplasmatic reticulum is an additional cellular target for hypothermic preservation, but that this may be avoided by oxygenation during preservation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
oxygenation during preservation may attenuate mitochondrial apoptosis, but may also induce ER‐stress, a phenomenon not seen with the use of simple oxygen insufflation.
oxygenation of the graft during preservation is an effective way to improve graft function after reperfusion.
oxygenation of perfusion media is a critical factor to consider in the development of machine perfusion protocols.
